business_question: Does the workspace understand quick entry, keep every tab in sync, and never lose an edit?

phases.name: business_understanding
phases.title: 1. Business Understanding
phases.objective: State the workspace's promises as things that can be measured.
phases.narrative: A task app earns trust through three behaviours users rarely see directly. What they type is understood. A change made in one tab appears in every other. And when two people change the same task at once, neither change vanishes without a trace. Each is tested here against the running application.
phases.gate_notes: Three measurable promises fixed before building the checks.

phases.name: data_understanding
phases.title: 2. Data Understanding
phases.objective: Decide what to test the parser and the server with.
phases.narrative: 60 phrases were written by hand against the documented grammar, including awkward ones: email addresses, issue numbers such as #3, impossible dates and markers with trailing punctuation. Because the same author wrote the parser and the phrases, 5,000 generated round trips provide a check that no phrase was chosen to pass.
phases.gate_notes: Test inputs fixed; their authorship stated.

phases.name: data_preparation
phases.title: 3. Data Preparation
phases.objective: Run every check against the real server on a throwaway database.
phases.narrative: The API is started as a subprocess on a free port with an empty temporary SQLite file, so the checks exercise the same code users run, and nothing persists between runs.

phases.name: modeling
phases.title: 4. Modeling
phases.objective: Build the grammar, the event stream and the version check.
phases.narrative: Quick entry is a small grammar resolved against an explicit date. Changes are written to SQLite and broadcast as server-sent events with a global sequence number, so a tab can tell whether it missed anything. Every update names the version it was based on; the store checks and writes under one lock.
phases.gate_notes: Three mechanisms, each with a test.

phases.name: evaluation
phases.title: 5. Evaluation
phases.narrative:
**Parsing.** 100.0% of labelled phrases were parsed exactly, against 28.3% for treating everything as the title; 0 of 5,000 round trips failed.

**Live updates.** With 50 tabs open, every tab received all 200 changes in order: yes. Delivery took 4.0 ms at the median and 14.8 ms at the 99th percentile.

**Conflicts.** In 50 rounds of 8 simultaneous edits, 50 were accepted and 350 refused; without the version check, each refused edit would have silently replaced another.
phases.gate_notes: All promises checked against the running server.

phases.name: deployment
phases.title: 6. Deployment
phases.narrative: FastAPI serves the tasks, analytics and event stream on port 8000; the React client keeps every view in sync from the stream and shows a conflict when an edit is refused.
phases.gate_notes: One server, one stream, every view.
